label: Сильный / Слабый
description: Сильный vs слабый: strong/weak contrasts across genders and everyday scenes.

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine nominative agreement. 'Сильный' takes the masculine ending to match 'ветер'. The weather phrase anchors the form in a common daily observation.
Strategic focus: Feminine nominative agreement. 'Слабая' takes the feminine ending to match 'память'. The sentence places the form in a familiar family context.
Strategic focus: Neuter nominative agreement. 'Слабое' takes the neuter ending to match 'здоровье'. The everyday concern makes the neuter form concrete.
Strategic focus: Plural nominative agreement. 'Сильные' takes the plural ending to match 'руки'. The vivid image fixes the plural form in mind.
Strategic focus: Direct masculine contrast. 'Сильный' is nominative for 'игрок' while 'слабого' is accusative for the animate 'соперника'. The match-up pairs both adjectives in one action.
Strategic focus: Masculine predicate adjective. 'Слабый' follows the noun as a predicate describing 'чай'. The everyday remark roots the form in daily life.
Strategic focus: Feminine instrumental in the predicate. After past-tense 'была', 'сильной' takes the feminine instrumental ending to match 'воля'. This shows the быть-plus-instrumental pattern.
Strategic focus: Plural instrumental in the predicate. After 'были', 'слабыми' takes the plural instrumental ending to match 'аргументы'. The sentence extends the pattern into the plural.
Strategic focus: Short-form masculine predicate. The short form 'силён' states a present quality of the subject with a vowel-fill 'ё'. Short forms are typical when describing a current state.
Strategic focus: Comparative form. 'Сильнее' is the comparative of 'сильный' and stays the same for any gender. The sentence compares today's coffee to the usual.
